skill.name: orchestration

skill.summary: Route and coordinate delegated AI tasks across multiple coding providers.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most backtick detections are Markdown formatting, but the guide intentionally invokes external AI CLIs, including automatic approval and write-capable modes. It also uses shared temporary worktrees, grants broad CLI permissions, and recommends wildcard cleanup that can affect user files. These behaviors require stronger approval, isolation, and cleanup controls.

remediation.issue: Broad pre-approved Bash permissions reduce command approval controls.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only exact read-only invocations, avoid automatic settings changes, and require explicit approval before write-capable or automatic-approval flags.

remediation.issue: Provider examples enable unattended write-capable execution.
remediation.suggestion: Keep every provider sandboxed and read-only by default, and gate workspace-write, yolo, force, and full-auto modes behind informed user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Predictable worktree paths are created and removed under a shared temporary directory.
remediation.suggestion: Create quoted paths with a secure unique-directory utility, then verify the path belongs to the controlled root before changing or removing it.

remediation.issue: Wildcard cleanup can remove pre-existing user files.
remediation.suggestion: Record exact files created by each delegated agent and remove only those paths after review or explicit user approval.

semantic_findings.description: The guide asks users to allow all Codex, Gemini, and Cursor Agent Bash invocations and offers automatic permission setup. Delegated tasks can then use write-capable commands without a fresh command approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The permission allowlist and automatic setup instruction are explicit. The same file documents write-capable and automatic-approval provider modes.

semantic_findings.title: Wildcard Cleanup Can Remove Unrelated Files
semantic_findings.description: The cleanup protocol directs deletion of files matching broad name patterns. Pre-existing user files such as matching analysis documents can be removed if incorrectly classified as agent-created.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The deletion instruction and wildcard patterns are explicit. The guide suggests checking new files, but it does not require exact creation tracking or user confirmation.

content.user_title: Orchestrate Tasks Across AI Coding Providers
content.value_statement: Coordinating several AI coding providers creates routing, isolation, and result collection work. This skill supplies documented workflows for invoking Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and Claude task agents.
actual_capabilities: Routes work among Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and Claude using task characteristics and provider strengths.
Documents read-only and write-mode CLI invocation patterns for supported external providers.
Launches provider tasks in the background and collects results through TaskOutput.
Defines fallback handling for authentication failures using interactive terminal sessions.
Recommends isolated Git worktrees for provider tasks requiring file changes.
Provides routing priorities and fallback chains for analysis, code execution, research, and quick generation.
limitations: This is documentation only and does not include executable orchestration scripts.
It requires installed provider CLIs, authenticated accounts, and Claude Code permission configuration.
Hard-coded provider models and flags may become outdated and must be verified with each CLI help output.
Write modes and automatic approval flags can modify files, so delegated work requires review and isolation.

use_cases.title: Run Parallel Code Reviews
use_cases.description: Send the same repository question to several providers, collect independent findings, and compare their conclusions.

use_cases.title: Design Provider Fallbacks
use_cases.description: Choose providers by context size, sandbox needs, speed, and task complexity, then define recovery paths for failures.

use_cases.title: Isolate Delegated Changes
use_cases.description: Place write-capable provider work in separate Git worktrees, inspect diffs, and merge only approved changes.

prompt_templates.title: Route a Read-Only Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [repository or files] using [provider]. Keep the provider read-only, run its help command first, and return findings without changing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a first delegated analysis with one provider.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Providers
prompt_templates.prompt: Run independent read-only reviews with Codex and Gemini for [task]. Collect both results, identify agreements and conflicts, then provide a concise synthesis.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when a second opinion can improve confidence.

prompt_templates.title: Isolate a Write Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an isolated worktree for [task]. Delegate implementation to [provider], show the diff, run [tests], and wait for approval before merging or cleanup.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for provider work that must change repository files.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Resilient Provider Chain
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [task] by complexity, context size, sandbox needs, and budget. Select a primary provider, define fallbacks, run suitable tasks in parallel, and synthesize results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for complex orchestration across several providers.

output_examples.input: Route a large, read-only architecture review.
output_examples.output: Primary provider: Gemini for large context. Mode: sandboxed and read-only. Fallback: Claude Opus. Result: a consolidated architecture review.

output_examples.input: Compare Codex and Cursor on a refactoring plan.
output_examples.output: Codex covers sandboxed implementation risks. Cursor covers multi-file edit strategy. The synthesis lists agreements, conflicts, and the recommended plan.

best_practices: Verify every provider CLI and current flags with its help output before invocation.
Keep read-only mode as default and require explicit approval before any write-capable or automatic-approval mode.
Use unique isolated worktrees, review diffs, and record exact cleanup targets before merging changes.
anti_patterns: Do not grant broad persistent CLI permissions when narrower, task-specific approval is available.
Do not place untrusted text directly into shell command strings or provider prompts without clear boundaries.
Do not delete files by wildcard or merge provider branches without reviewing ownership and changes.

faq.question: Does this skill include runnable scripts?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation, command patterns, routing guidance, and workflow examples.

faq.question: Which providers does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Claude task agents, OpenAI Codex, Google Gemini, and Cursor Agent.

faq.question: Does it modify files by default?
faq.answer: The guide declares read-only mode as default. Some examples enable writes or automatic approval, so verify each final command.

faq.question: How are authentication failures handled?
faq.answer: The workflow opens an interactive terminal for provider login, waits for completion, and retries the native invocation.

faq.question: Can provider tasks run in parallel?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide shows background Task calls for several providers and TaskOutput calls for result collection.

faq.question: How should provider output be accepted?
faq.answer: Compare results, inspect file diffs, run relevant tests, and merge only changes that pass human review.
